the rendering rule (2026-09-17): a record accessor that counts its own calls instead of throwing - expected outcome is rendered without executing, the backing field read directly

the rendering rule (2026-09-17): an ArrayList subclass whose overridden iterator() counts its calls and refuses - expected outcome is rendered without executing, through the platform ancestor's own state
the rendering rule (2026-09-17): a user Collection implemented from scratch, not a platform-collection subclass - expected outcome is rendered without executing its own iterator()

the rendering rule's 2026-09-18 refinement: a subclass of the ABSTRACT platform base AbstractMap, whose overridden entrySet() counts its calls and refuses - no honest ancestor state read exists, so expected outcome is object-introspected without executing the override

the rendering rule's 2026-09-18 refinement: a subclass of the ABSTRACT platform base AbstractCollection, whose overridden iterator() counts its calls and refuses - expected outcome is object-introspected without executing the override

the rendering rule holds on BOTH rendering paths, not only the flat one: the same user Collection implemented from scratch, replayed through the structured renderer - expected outcome is rendered without executing its own iterator(), on the structured path too

the rendering rule: a composite never renders through its own toString, on either path - a FIELDLESS user subclass of the ABSTRACT platform base AbstractCollection declares no state of its own, so a stateless leaf's stringification exemption would let it stand behind its own text, but that text is the inherited AbstractCollection.toString(), which walks the overridden iterator() - expected outcome is the type name (no field to dump), the override never called, no failure marker

the rendering rule: a FIELDLESS class overriding toString() holds its real state off the reflectable-field graph, in a static identity-keyed side table - the stateless-leaf exemption would let it stand behind its own text, but that text reads the side table's secret state, invisible to field reflection - expected outcome is the type name (no field to dump), the side table never consulted, no failure marker

the rendering rule: a composite never renders through its own toString, on either path - a user Number subclass carrying a deny-listed field is a composite that merely extends a numeric base, and the flat path's scalar-numeric fast path read its own text (only the value-shape scan and the length cap in front of it, no field name for the deny-list to match) while the structured path introspected the same value and hid the field - expected outcome is the field walk on both channels alike, the type named and the secret redacted, never its own text
